title: AI Engineering Framework V2.1 Master
subtitle: Universal Agentic Architecture: Spec-as-Code Governance, Modular Adapters (Claw Code Rust, Ollama), WSCI & Jidoka
summary: Universal agentic engineering constitution decoupled with a Modular Adapter layer (Claw Code CLI in Rust, Model Ollama, Git Worktrees), plugin ecosystem (Everything Claude Code, Karpathy Guidelines, Ruflo, Superpowers), Spec-as-Code governance, and automated bootstrap.
overview:
The revolution of Artificial Intelligence in software development brought agility, but also revealed a major risk: treating autonomous agents as 'magical code generators', which often leads to brittle codebases, silent regressions, and a loss of governance. To solve this deep challenge in modern software engineering, I created the AI Engineering Framework V2.1 Master — a Universal Constitution for Agentic Engineering.

The central goal was to engineer a tool-agnostic governance architecture capable of orchestrating LLMs throughout the software development lifecycle. The solution establishes strict boundaries between intent (defined by humans in META_SPEC), execution, and verification. I implemented a structured lifecycle called SPARC+DD (Discovery, Specification, Pseudocode, Architecture, Refinement, Completion, Deployment, Documentation) and adopted the Declarative Pointers technique to integrate documentation without data duplication. With this, AI acts not as an unguided substitute, but as a surgical force multiplier of engineering capabilities.
roleDescription: As AI Solutions Architect & Tech Lead, I defined the strategic, conceptual, and architectural design of the framework:
responsibilities: Governance Design: Created the finite state machine (Bootstrap ➡️ Discovery ➡️ Foundation ➡️ Execution ➡️ Checkpoint) ensuring human developer authority at critical gates (Gate_1_Review).
Context Engineering (WSCI): Defined the context management methodology (Write, Select, Compress, Isolate) to prevent hallucinations caused by context poisoning or distraction.
Multi-Agent Topology: Architected separation of responsibilities among virtual agents (Analyst, Architect, Developer, QA), enforcing the principle of Least Privilege.

i18n Architecture: Developed the 'Single Source of Truth + Localized Mirror' solution, keeping canonical documentation in English for AI technical precision while localized mirrors in Portuguese serve human stakeholders.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: Balancing the canonical context required for artificial intelligence models with information consumption by local engineering teams without creating duplicate documentation or single-source-of-truth conflicts.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Engineered the Declarative Pointers strategy, keeping canonical files such as META_SPEC.md and ADRs unmodified in their source locations (in English) while creating a Localized Mirror layer (docs/pt-br/) for human consumption.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: Excessive agent autonomy causing speculative unauthorized refactorings and silent regressions.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Formalized the Think Before Coding discipline and mandatory anchoring of every creative or modifying action to a verifiable Checkpoint, enforcing Evidence Before Assumption and strictly Surgical Changes.

futureEvolution: Implementation of automated CI/CD hooks to natively validate governance state machine Checkpoints prior to allowing merges.
Creation of telemetry metrics derived from reasoning layer logs (Plan Mode) to optimize context tokenization for LLMs.

owaspMitigations.title: Injection (Prompt Injection Boundary)
owaspMitigations.description: Strict enforcement that all retrieved external content (RAG, Web, Issues) is treated purely as untrusted data without instructional authority, shielding the framework from malicious prompt injection.

owaspMitigations.title: Broken Access Control (Security by Default & Least Privilege)
owaspMitigations.description: Adoption of a segregated permissions matrix. Analysis agents are restricted to strict Read-Only access, while infrastructure agents require explicit human authorization for destructive actions.
